body.objective: Students will be able to read and follow a project plan.
body.iCan: I can read and follow a project plan.
successCriteria: I can read a project plan and materials list
I can measure accurately and follow steps in order
I can track my progress and solve problems as I work
body.hook: A carpenter's saying goes: "Measure twice, cut once." In every CTS area, from foods to construction to fashion, the plan is what turns materials into a finished product without wasting time or money.

vocabulary.definition: A document listing the steps, materials and tools needed to complete a project.
A list of every material and quantity needed.
Finding size, amount or quantity using tools such as rulers or measuring cups.
The allowable difference from an exact measurement.
The final surface treatment or presentation of a product.

study.title: Follow the Plan
study.question: How do I follow a plan to complete a quality project?
study.passage:
Choose a starter project for your CTS area (teacher provides the plan):
• Foods: a batch of muffins (recipe = plan)
• Construction: a small wooden box or bookend
• Fashion: a drawstring bag
• Design or communications: a printed event poster from a template
• Computing: a simple webpage from a wireframe
Part 1, Read the whole plan (10 minutes): Before touching anything, read every step. Highlight safety notes, circle unfamiliar words and look them up.
Part 2, Gather (10 minutes): Check off each item on the materials and tools list. Mise en place (everything in place) is used by chefs and works in every shop.
Part 3, Measure (10 minutes): Practise with the right tools: dry vs liquid measuring cups, tape measure to 1 mm, seam allowance gauge. Know the tolerance: a box joint may allow ±1 mm, a muffin recipe ±5 g of flour.
Part 4, Build (40 minutes or across classes): Follow steps in order. Tick each step on a progress log with the time and any problems.
Part 5, Finish and clean (10 minutes): Apply the finish, clean the work area and return tools.

examples.title: Read first
examples.problem: Why read every step before starting a recipe?
examples.answer: Some steps need preparation, like preheating the oven or soaking materials
examples.explore: What could go wrong if you don't?

examples.title: Measuring
examples.problem: How do you measure flour accurately?
examples.answer: Spoon flour into a dry measuring cup and level it with a straight edge

examples.title: Tolerance

examples.answer: Step 6: seam crooked; didn't use guide; unpicked and re-sewed with the seam guide

practice.a: Check measurements before cutting to avoid waste.
